content.title: About
content.content: Seafood paella is a classic Spanish dish made with Bomba rice, olive oil, saffron, vegetables and a mix of seafood such as shrimp, mussels, squid and fish. The dish is known for its aromatic broth and the crispy bottom layer called “socarrat.”

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Paella originates from Valencia, where it is traditionally cooked over an open fire in a wide, shallow pan called a “paellera.”
Saffron, which gives the dish its golden hue, is one of the most expensive spices in the world.
The original Valencian paella uses local ingredients: chicken, rabbit, garbanzo beans and green beans “ferra.”
The seafood version is called “paella de marisco” and is popular in coastal regions of Spain.
Paella is often a communal dish, prepared for celebrations and family gatherings.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Seafood (shrimp, mussels, squid, fish) provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Fish and shellfish contain EPA and DHA, which support cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Bomba rice is a slow‑digesting carbohydrate that offers steady blood‑sugar levels and lasting satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Thanks to the seafood and saffron, the dish supplies B12, niacin and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Paella provides iron, zinc, selenium and iodine, nutrients that aid the immune system and thyroid function.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels or fish.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Broths and seasonings can be salty; people with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Heavy metals
items.content: Certain seafood can accumulate cadmium or mercury; purchase from reputable sources.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish is relatively calorie‑rich due to oil and rice, so portions should be moderated for weight control.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve paella hot, straight from the pan. Eat with a fork or spoon, mixing rice with the seafood. It is often garnished with lemon wedges, fresh parsley and a pinch of smoked paprika.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat with a splash of broth or water to restore moisture. Freeze only for up to 1 month after cooling the dish completely.
